To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
justice is an objective measure that aims to increase fairness among employees in the family business.
the family business literature has developed independently from the organizational justice literature, which has resulted in a lack of clarity about the concepts of fairness and justice.

the family business literature has so far used the concepts of justice (objective measures that aim to create fairness) and fairness (perceptions) interchangeably, which is problematic because the two concepts have different theoretical foundations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to increase fairness in the family business workforce and how to maintain an ethical workplace in the family business.
the role of fairness perceptions among family employees, as well as the role of family business leaders in building and maintaining an ethically sound family business workplace.
how family businesses should balance their economic and socioemotional goals in their pursuit to increase justice in their workplace.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the family business literature should not only be concerned with the concept of justice, but also with fairness perceptions among employees.
justice is a prerequisite for fairness.
justice is the objective, rational and fair treatment of employees, while fairness is the subjective, emotional and perceived fair treatment of employees.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the family business literature has to be aware of the potential conflict between justice and fairness in the family business context, and that it is important to incorporate socioemotional goals into justice-related rules and regulations in order to increase fairness perceptions in the workplace.
justice and fairness should be viewed as two distinct constructs that can come into conflict, especially in the family business setting.

family business owners and managers should be aware of the fact that the utilitarian conceptualization and application of justice in the family workplace may lead to a decrease in fairness perceptions among employees.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a utilitarian approach to justice may be at odds with family values and socioemotional wealth in family businesses
family business scholars and practitioners need to pay more attention to how the family business workplace can be designed and managed in a way that is both just and fair.
a focus on fairness is needed to ensure a healthy family business workplace.
